title: Starling Launches Agentic AI Assistant for Business
summary:
Starling Bank has today launched an agentic AI-powered ‘Starling Assistant’ to all business customers. The free in-app tool has been designed to boost productivity and cut admin by helping small businesses manage their day-to-day transactions, detect and avoid scams, and plan ahead using personalised financial insights. 
Starling Assistant goes beyond a standard Q&A by executing complex banking commands — acting as a proactive partner. Its capabilities include:
Tax Ring-Fencing: Business owners can issue direct commands to streamline tax management, such as asking the assistant: “Put 20% of last month’s earnings aside for VAT.” The assistant will calculate the figure from the account history and transfer the funds safely into a dedicated Space.
Invoice Fraud and Scam Defence: SMEs can talk to the assistant about invoices from suppliers and it can flag potential scams, advising what action the business owner should take. For example, if payment details have changed the company should be contacted directly to confirm if they are accurate. In 2025, invoice fraud cost businesses over £41m, according to UK Finance.
Making Tax Digital (MTD) Navigator: This helps sole traders and landlords understand their MTD for Income Tax obligations. The assistant will ask questions on income levels and tell users when they are likely to be mandated for MTD. It can also share links to HMRC and gives taxpayers instructions on what to do on HMRC's website, e.g. double check if they are mandated and where to sign up.
Receipt Tracker: Business owners can already add receipts to their transactions, and later this year Starling Assistant will be able to analyse and extract financial information seamlessly. Businesses will be able to track spending for specific jobs by asking queries e.g. “Summarise the amount I’ve spent on paint in the last week from receipts.” The AI will cross-reference the transaction history with the data extracted from the receipt to provide an accurate, instant breakdown. 
“We know that managing finances can be a major drain on time for small businesses,” said Harriet Rees, Group Chief Information Officer at Starling. “Starling Assistant changes this by automating routine tasks and taking the guesswork out of money management. We’re committed to boosting SME productivity, as Starling’s own research shows that if more small businesses adopted digital financial tools their growth could add £25.3bn to the UK economy.”
Looking ahead, Starling plans to expand the tool’s capabilities significantly. Later this year, Starling Assistant will be fully integrated with Starling’s Accounting software. This will help businesses effortlessly manage cash flow by instructing the assistant to create and send invoices directly to customers on their behalf. The bank will add a new tool to the Assistant every week for the rest of the year, and customers can request new tools for Starling’s AI team to build.*

title: Viva.com Signs Cyprus State Payment Services Contract
summary:
Viva.com, the first Tech Bank in Europe for businesses, has been awarded by the Treasury of the Republic of Cyprus the contract to provide electronic transaction processing services for the Cypriot state. In doing so, Viva.com will set up an advanced payments infrastructure for the Cypriot state, reinforcing its position as a pan-European critical banking infrastructure that combines scale with local expertise, serving both public institutions and businesses across Europe.
The contract covers electronic payments made by citizens and businesses to the Cypriot state, including direct taxes, vehicle license renewals, and social insurance contributions, with total managed payment volume expected to exceed €1,5 billion annually.
Under the agreement, Viva.com will provide the Cypriot State with a modern, multi-channel electronic transaction processing infrastructure. The new platform gives citizens more ways to pay, combining card and account-to-account (A2A) payments, while providing the State with a more efficient way to process transactions. Viva.com will act as the backbone processing engine behind Cyprus's Payment Gateway (PGW) via the Gov.cy platform, centralising electronic payments and allowing citizens to settle all their obligations to government departments and services through a single platform.
Viva.com will be responsible for the management of all online transactions via its Smart Checkout payment solution, and the procurement, installation and maintenance of all physical card-acceptance (POS) terminals featuring its Tap on Any Device technology, across Cyprus's public services. 
The award follows Viva.com's selection in July by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union (DG TAXUD) - in partnership with European Dynamics, a leading eGovernment and digital transformation company -, to build and operate the central payment platform behind the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), covering all 27 member states from 2027 - one of the EU’s flagship climate initiatives. 
Harry Xenophontos, Chief Business Officer, Viva.com, commented:

KeyPoint saw the moment as more than a routine technology upgrade, and set out to find an AI platform that could understand context, hold intelligent, human-like conversations, and improve every member interaction. The goal went beyond modernizing the contact center, toward investing in an AI foundation that could scale and serve members for years to come.
After evaluating multiple top-tier vendors, KeyPoint expanded its Eltropy deployment to include AI Voice and AI Chat alongside Appointment Management, replacing scripted interactions with AI that retrieves information in real time and handles both authenticated and unauthenticated inquiries.
“This has the ability to change our member experience in a really positive way,” said Josh Herzog, VP of Operations Experience & Payments at KeyPoint Credit Union.
Building a New Authentication Path Together
KeyPoint also pushed the deployment past a standard implementation. Working alongside Eltropy's team, KeyPoint helped design a debit card-based authentication workflow, a capability that had not previously been deployed at any financial institution. The two teams built the verification experience to meet KeyPoint's high standards while keeping the process simple enough for members to adopt from day one.
Measurable Results Within a Month
The impact showed up quickly. Voice service levels climbed from 75% to 87% in KeyPoint's first month with the expanded deployment, while chat service levels improved as well. Eltropy AI resolved 92% of chat inquiries and nearly 93% of voice inquiries, keeping the majority of routine questions from ever reaching a live agent and giving KeyPoint leadership confidence that members were getting accurate answers, not just faster ones.
With fewer repetitive inquiries landing on the frontline, KeyPoint's contact center team has more time for the conversations that call for a human, while members can get answers whenever they need them.
What Comes Next
KeyPoint's next step is rolling out an internal knowledge base so staff can get instant answers to policy and procedure questions instead of tracking down a colleague by phone, email or Teams. Beyond that, the credit union is preparing for agentic AI to take on more of the work itself, such as an AI agent that transcribes a member's call in real time, opens a dispute case automatically, and texts the member a case number before they hang up.
“It's reimagining how work gets done,” Herzog said. “What if I could give you hours back every week? That's not replacing you, but just reimagining what your role is.”
"KeyPoint asked for a way to authenticate members that didn't exist yet, and we built it with them," said Ashish Garg, CEO and Co-Founder of Eltropy. "Now every credit union on our Agentic AI Platform has access to it."
